My own phrase queries returned the same scanned fragments A stitched together: 'Pitch characterizes words in Ugandan Bantu languages in much the same way as stress characterizes words in English', 'of the Ugandan Bantu languages, each vowel in a word has to be marked as having one [of two basic pitch possibilities (tones)]', the En…
new_statements.relation_note: Group-level: Ugandan Bantu languages incl. Lukenyi have two-tone systems on every vowel; tone-marking conventions for the wordlists; lexical-similarity and phonological-feature tables that include a Lukenyi column.
new_statements.rule_in_words: The Ugandan Bantu languages surveyed (Lukenyi among them) are treated as tone languages: every vowel bears one of two tones (H acute, L grave, falling circumflex), pitch being a property of each word much as stress is in English; lexical minimal pairs by pitch are few. No statement about word stress in these languages; nothing specific to Lukenyi beyond its inclusion in the sample.
new_statements.exceptions: hedged as 'probably' and 'most of the Ugandan Bantu languages'; long vowels may carry two like or unlike pitches; 'rising tones do not occur within a syllable' (snippet); consonants 'also have distinctive tones on some occasions' (Luganda long consonants)
new_statements.identity_note: The book's own sample includes 'Lukenyi' alongside Luganda, Lusoga, Lugwere, Lunyole, Lugwe, Lusamia, Lumasaba, Ruruli (snippets: 'consider Luganda, Lusoga and Lukenyi to be merely different dialects of one language'; similarity row 'Lukenyi 79 83'; 'bone.. in Lukenyi is eigomba'), so Lukenyi = Kenyi lke of Lake Kyoga. The tone statement recovered is a generalisation over 'most of the Ugandan Bantu languages', not a Kenyi-specific sentence; whether the appendix wordlist carries tone marks for the Lukenyi column could not be verified.

sources.note: Lulamogi is reported (Ethnologue 2016) as mutually intelligible with Kenye; Hyman's Lulamogi papers are the nearest first-hand prosodic description (tone: H vs zero, boundary tones) and may comment on Lukenyi; not a Kenyi source but the best proxy.
